emulators.latest_body:
## 1.1.3 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- **Fast precision is as light as the older versions again.** Its pixel
  shaders still did per-pixel work added for the exact mode (rounding every
  step to the console's bytes, holding coordinates on texel edges, a pass
  per sample on antialiased surfaces), which made full-screen effects up to
  half again as expensive. At higher internal resolutions on integrated and
  older GPUs that was the difference between full speed and half
  (Midnight Club 3 at 3x). Fast now costs the same as 1.0.104 or less.
- Fast precision: stray lines over Vice City's buildings.
- Log lines and environment variables say xbased (`XBASED_*`; the older
  `HAKUX_*` names still work). For LAN play every machine needs 1.1.3.

releases.name: xbased 1.1.2
releases.body:
## 1.1.2 (2026-11)

### New
- **GPU precision** (Settings › System, or per game): **Exact** draws with
  the console graphics chip's own arithmetic, the closest to a real Xbox and
  the heaviest on the GPU; **Fast** uses plain float shaders, as xbased did
  up to 1.0.94, much lighter on the GPU. **Automatic**, the
  default, picks Fast on AMD Polaris and Vega cards and Vega integrated
  graphics (their driver crashed building the exact shaders), on CPUs of 4
  threads or fewer, and from the next run on a GPU that crashed building a
  shader, took too long to build the exact ones or could not keep up with
  them; Exact everywhere else. The setting's help shows what Automatic
  chose last and why.
- **Cached shaders built before the game** is on by default, in both
  precisions.

### Fixes
- No more shader stutter on GPUs without pipeline libraries (AMD's Windows
  driver, older Intel drivers): the hybrid mode can't run there and fell
  back to synchronous builds, pausing the game for every new shader; it now
  builds them in the background.
- On CPUs with few threads, shader builds no longer take time from the
  game: they run below its threads and only on the threads it leaves free

releases.name: xbased 1.1.1
releases.body:
## 1.1.1 (2026-11)

### New
- **Online mode**, per game (Mods & patches): the game runs as the console
  does for playing online (Insignia, XLink Kai, System Link), at its
  original frame rate and speed, without patches, mods or cheats, and fast
  forward does nothing. Insignia bans players who use them.
- **Interface in 4:3** (Settings › Interface): the menus in a centered 4:3
  area, for bezels and frame shaders over a 4:3 picture.
- **Import saves from a folder** (Memory, Tab): saves copied from an Xbox or
  from xemu, re-signed with the keys of xemu's own files (and, for saves
  locked to another console, that console's eeprom.bin in the folder). The
  import from xemu also finds more games' signatures.
- **Discs from an NBD server**: `nbd://host:port/export` as the disc, the way
  GDOX serves a physical disc from a supported drive.
- **Command line**: `-h` / `--help`, `-c` / `--config FILE` for another
  settings file, `-i` / `--input FILE` for the disc.
- The game window keeps its place and size for the next game (Windows).

- Alt+Tab out of a game no longer leaves Alt held (the F keys did noth

releases.name: xbased 1.1.0
releases.body:
## 1.1.0 (2026-11)

### New
- **Hybrid shader compilation**, the new default: a shader a game hasn't
  used before is drawn at once by interpreter shaders while its own is
  built in the background, so games no longer stutter while shaders
  compile, even on a first run with an empty cache. Settings › System ›
  New shaders also offers the asynchronous and synchronous modes. Updating
  switches every install to hybrid once; your choice after that stays.
- **Aspect ratio Auto**: 16:9 for games that render in widescreen, 4:3 for
  the rest, and save states remember each game's shape.
- **Screenshots and save state thumbnails as JPEG**, much smaller files.
- xbased.exe's file properties show the real version.

### Graphics
- Graphics chip accuracy, from the chip test program (nxdk_pgraph_tests):
  2959 of its 3556 pictures now match the console's exactly (1103 in
  1.0.104). One accurate base for every game, Direct3D titles included:
  lighting, vertex programs, fog and depth computed with the chip's own
  arithmetic; lines, points, outlines and smoothed edges; W-buffering;
  texture filtering, DXT, YUV, bump and shadow map sampling; multisampling,
  anisotropic filtering, logic ops a

releases.name: v2.5.0
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).
- **An experimental SDL3 frontend**, `a2sdl3

### Changed

- The automatic choice of the recording thread (`RPS5E_GPU_RECORD_THREAD=auto`) no longer turns it off while the command interpreter also has to wait for room in its queue (`RPS5E_POLICY_FULL`). ### Fixed

- Frame captures (`RPS5E_CAPTURE_FRAMES`) of GTA V replay again instead of hanging the GPU. While a capture recorded, GPU results copied straight into guest memory were later taken for CPU writes and recorded; the replay wrote them over its own GPU results, which differ where GPU work orders its atomics differently, and the mixed ray-tracing tree sent a shader into an endless loop. GPU results now reach guest memory through copies the capture sees while it records.

  system call. Found by Napomex.
- **Saving is safer.** When a game erased all of its save memory, the built-in BIOS did not wait
  for the cartridge to finish and could freeze the game. It now waits like the real BIOS. This
  affects Ki

# NgpCraft Emulator v3.12 - what's new

New features, netplay fix attempt. **If you play mirror matches online,
both players must update**: this version cannot play a mirror match with 3.9.1 or older.

## New features

- **Updates from inside the emulator.** *Settings ▸ General ▸ Check for updates* tells you if a
  newer version is out. On Windows and Linux, *Install and restart* downloads it, installs it and
  starts it: no more trip to the GitHub page. On macOS the button opens the download page. The
  emulator also checks by itself at startup, at most once a day, and never interrupts a game

  download by hand.**
- **Run-ahead (optional, off by default).** *Settings ▸ General ▸ Run-ahead*: shows the picture the

  the game itself disappears from the screen. In *Sonic*, a jump now shows up 4 frames after the

NgpCraft Emulator v3.9.0 - what's new
This release is about playing two players over the internet. It is still being tested, but the
first results are encouraging. If you play online, both of you should update, and please tell us
how it goes.

Online play in mirror mode should be smoother
Less input lag at the start of a match. The player who finished loading first used to start alone and wait for the other one. That wait made the emulator think the connection was slower than it really was, and it could add noticeable delay to that player's controls for several minutes. Both sides now start together. This idea comes from Blueteemo, who proposed it in pull request #26. Thank you!
Fewer freezes on a connection that loses packets. Your button presses are now also sent a second way, repeated several times, so a single lost packet should no longer freeze both screens. In our tests on a deliberately bad connection, most of the short freezes went away.
If the other player has an older version, the match should still work, just without these improvements.

releases.body:
# Zaxnes 0.4.0

Independent project, not affiliated with Geod Studio or Nintendo. NES is a trademark of Nintendo.

## New

- **Widescreen.** Games made for it, or patched for it, draw past the 256 pixels of the NES picture, in 2D and in 3D. Built-in widescreen hacks for Zelda II, Mega Man 1 to 6, Super Mario Bros., Super Mario Bros. 3, Castlevania, Ninja Gaiden III, Adventure Island, Excitebike, Final Fantasy, Blaster Master, Metroid and Metal Force (Korea), each in a plain and an advanced mode (objects and enemies shown in the margins). The hacks are found by the ROM's signatures, so other builds (Europe, Japan) of these games are covered where a pack exists. releases.body:
**Fixed: "POM2 is damaged" on macOS.** An accented file name in the package
broke the app's signature when the Finder copied it into *Applications*. macOS
then called the app damaged and offered no way to allow it from System Settings.

The emulator itself is unchanged from
[v1.1.0](https://github.com/habib256/pom2/releases/tag/v1.1.0), which has the
full list of new features. v1.1.1 was tagged but never published.

releases.name: POM2 v1.1.0
releases.body:
**New hardware.** Eight cards — Microsoft SoftCard II, PCPI Applicard,
Premium SoftCard //e, ALS CP/M Card, Saturn 128K, Videx UltraTerm, DAN ][
Controller, E-Z Color (TMS9918A, with its own Card Monitor tab) — and an
OS-call trace (ProDOS MLI, SmartPort, Pascal BIOS, Monitor, CP/M BDOS, …).

**No copyrighted firmware ships.** A Disk II boots on POM2's own boot PROM
and data separator; a first launch offers to download the rest.

**Closer to the silicon.** All 801 comments that cite MAME or AppleWin were
re-read against the primary sources — datasheets, Sather, Apple's technical
notes, format specifications, ROM disassemblies — in 33 reports under
`docs/audits/`. Where POM2 and those sources disagreed, 3 major and 26 minor
fixes followed: a `SAVE` that disarmed the //c motor timer, a 6551 IRQ the
datasheet does not allow, a Z8530 write that stopped the transmitter, a FLUX
track losing one transition per revolution, a same-value 6522 store that
re-strobed the AY, five ImageWriter power-on defaults. Where POM2's reading
of a datasheet differs from another emulator's, the divergence is now
documented in the code rather than silently aligned. Every hardware claim
carries its **evidence

releases.name: POM2 v1.0.0
releases.body:
The first stable release: the Apple ][, ][+, //e, //c and //c Plus, in NTSC
and PAL, with the cards, media and tools listed in the README.

- **Your data stays put:** an unreadable `state.cfg`, a disk on an unplugged
  drive, the printouts of a second window and the browser's saved sessions
  are no longer lost.
- **Accelerators keep real time:** video, Disk II, SoftCard, Liron and
  paddles stay at 1 MHz under a TransWarp, a Zip or the //c Plus.
- **Closer to the hardware:** composite colour, `.nib` sync, SSI263 speech,
  paddle timers and the ][+ cursor.
- **Bundled disks:** A2 File Cmd 1.0, Dirtbike 1.1, ChromaBreak 1.1,
  Micro-Sokoban 1.3 and DIX.
- **macOS:** relative paths and the first launch of a downloaded copy work.
- **Many fixes** from bug hunts against MAME, AppleWin and the data sheets.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/habib256/pom2/compare/v0.9.9...v1.0.0)

releases.name: POM2 v0.9.9
releases.body:
- **Browser:** `?url=` boots a disk image from another site, the screen
  opens on its own, and the audio no longer crackles.
- **Input:** the host mouse can drive paddles 0 and 1, and the //e
  Shift-key mod is an option.
- **Disks:** choose a disk's sector order by hand, format a WOZ on any
  track, and a macOS command-line disk boots once.
- **//c and //c Plus:** Ctrl-Reset keeps the 3.5-inch drives, and SmartPort
  calls answer like the Liron firmware.
- **Accuracy:** WDC `WAI`, the ThunderClock interrupt from power-up, and a
  cassette recording that follows the rewind.
- **Proven on real software:** DIX, Arlequin and Extasie on the Féline, and

- **`pom2_core` SDK:** the //c and //c Plus, the mouse, a bus watch and the

The first release of Odin.

Odin (ᚨ) is a low-level emulator of the SEGA Hikaru arcade board. It runs the programs of the real chips wherever they are known, and draws with OpenGL or Vulkan. It is a hard fork of Valkyrie, by Stefano Teso.

**First public preview — Windows x64 and experimental Linux x86-64**

VKRT NES Remaster is an open-source, native C++20 Nintendo Entertainment System emulator developed by Francisco Triemstra (VKRT).

releases.body:
**Lumen Emu 0.1.7, build 10** updates the GitHub APK with a quick folder browser, direct access to your existing game library, PS4 audio fixes and the latest cumulative core changes.

### Library and interface

- Choose your game folder quickly and use its files in place after granting Android’s all-files access. No private copy is required for the GitHub APK.
- Preserve the selected folder from earlier direct-access GitHub releases, together with existing settings and saves. The one-time folder reset used by the Play migration is skipped on GitHub.
- English dashboard and folder-selection flow, with an expanded compatibility catalog.
- Updated device-specific compatibility reports in the README, including developer-reported West of Dead version 01.00 on realme GT 8 Pro. Reports remain tied to their stated device and tested build.

### Audio and core

- Improve NGS2 streamed PCM audio, buffer completion callbacks and voice-state queries. The corrected path restored audible Brotato audio in the documented Android development test.
- Integrate six selected KytyPS5 improvements to shader compilation, shader identity and memory-range handling while preserving Lumen’s existing defaults.

releases.name: Lumen Emu 0.1.6 — Faster loading, Banners & automatic PanVK
releases.body:
## Massive loading improvements and experimental Mali support

**Lumen Emu 0.1.6 brings a massive loading speedup in the tested PS5 startup path, restores direct local-ROM access for both PS4 and PS5, bundles Turnip Banners, and adds automatic experimental PanVK selection for compatible Mali GPUs.**

### Faster loading

- Local ROM folders now use direct filesystem reads after granting Android's all-files access, avoiding repeated document-provider work during loading.
- The system folder picker remains available. Recognised local filesystem folders use the direct path; other supported providers retain the document bridge.
- Document-backed libraries also benefit from reduced path lookups, provider acquisition and directory-enumeration overhead, plus improved native file-size queries.

releases.body:
# Changes
* Fix controller presence detection in RMG-Input-GCA (thank you @EIREXE)
* Use SDL GUID in RMG-Input (thank you @bmsuseluda)
* Add mupen64plus-video-softrdp plugin (thank you @PixelMechanic0 for the suggestion)
* Update mupen64plus-core, mupen64plus-video-GLideN64, SDL_GameControllerDB and LZMA SDK

# Changes
* Fix build issues with zlib v1.3.1
* Fix audio not working when using the AppImage (thank you @Samueru-sama)
* Fix screenshots causing a crash on Linux
* Remove dispatcher server support
* Update mupen64plus-core and LZMA SDK

# Notes
The netplay servers hosted by @loganmc10 have been changed into something incompatible with RMG, due to these changes RMG will no longer have any hosted servers, but self-hosting isn't too difficult as I've outlined in the new netplay section in the README.

# Changes
* Fix AppImage icon not working since v0.7.1 (thank you @Samueru-sama)
* Fix desktop file causing a crash on Budgie (thank you @jpleatherland)
* Fix memory pak from player 2, 3 and 4 not saving correctly (see https://github.com/mupen64plus/mupen64plus-core/commit/3c2955c910d535b3da7721c66b5b8e01b3361160)
* Fix Star Wars - Rogue Squadron having missing geometry when using GLideN64 (see https://github.com/gonetz/GLideN64/issues/2950)
* Remove translations from the configuration GUI of GLideN64 (see https://github.com/gonetz/GLideN64/pull/2954)
* Add plugin settings shortcuts to the toolbar
* Update mupen64plus-video-GLideN64, SDL_net and SDL_GameControllerDB

# Changes
* Fix exit confirmation dialog showing when launching RMG with '--nogui'
* Fix emulation not shutting down properly on exit in some cases
* Fix remaining issues with the 'Auto-Configure' button state in the configuration dialog of RMG-Input
* Fix asserts being enabled when building the RelWithDebInfo configuration
* Fix uninitialized variable being read in the configuration dialog of GLideN64
* Add checkbox to drag and drop confirmation dialog to prevent future confirmations
* Move 'Ask for confirmation on exit' setting to the emulation tab in the settings dialog
* Improve 'Input Device' UI element in the configuration GUI of RMG-Input by allowing it to take more width
* Improve refresh and join button state in the Netplay Session Browser dialog

# Changes
* Fix drag and drop not working in the flatpak
* Fix hotkeys dialog in RMG-Input not showing native face button names
* Fix cheat dialog in RMG not allowing users to set cheat option since v0.7.2
* Fix cheat codes not being cleared before trying to load another cheat in RMG-Core
* Fix 'Auto-Configure' button being enabled when it should be disabled after configuring a button
* Fix top row of UI elements in the configuration GUI of RMG-Input not being aligned properly
* Add tooltips to the top row of UI elements in the configuration GUI of RMG-Input
* Add 'Game Type' to the 'ROM Information' dialog

releases.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo 1.10.2
releases.body:
## Mario Kart 8 Deluxe online fixed (2306-0502)
- 1.10.0 started deferring every Bsd poll with a finite timeout. That broke the NEX connection of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which failed with error 2306-0502. MK8's ordinary NEX polls now use the blocking path again, as in 1.9.9; eventfd polls and the finite-timeout optimization of other games (Portal 2 and others) are unchanged (#75)

## New online games
- SpeedRunners 2: Nextendo routes scoped to the game, and a TLS peer reset during the handshake is now returned to the game as an SSL error instead of stopping the emulator (#79)
- Just Dance 2022: Nextendo routes, exact-build TLS trust patch with native certificate verification kept on, and blocking UDP receives no longer hold the shared socket thread (#74)
- Ultimate Chicken Horse 1.13.13.765: online support (#68)
- Guilty Gear Strive: online services redirected to Nextendo (#77)
- Nintendo Switch Online Classics: versions set for NES, SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Advance, Nintendo 64 and SEGA Genesis, plus a Windows JIT fix (#69)

## Other fixes
- Steam Deck: touchscreen, rumble and gyro input (#76)
- NPLN online patches are loaded from the signed patch catalog (#73)
- nim: the IShopServic

releases.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo 1.10.1
releases.body:
## Friends
- The friend list filter of a game (online, same game, favorites) is now applied before the list is cut to the game's buffer, so a game asking for friends in the same game gets them.
- A friend is "in the same game" only when their presence names the game you are playing.
- The friend panel and the "Friend online" notification show the name of the game, using the name sent by the Nextendo server when the title is unknown locally.
- Splatoon 3 and Portal 2 added to the game name table.

## Also in this version (from 1.10.0)
- Portal 2: online menus and the co-op lobby run at full speed, crash after a failed join fixed, 1.0.3 required online.
- Network: a socket wait with a time limit no longer blocks the other network calls of the game.
- Game version table: Minecraft 1.0.17 and Portal 2 1.0.3.

## Update
- The built-in updater offers this version (Help > Check for Updates, or System Update in the HOME Menu) and keeps your portable folder: keys, saves and account stay in place.

releases.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo 1.10.0 | Aperture Science Update
releases.body:
## Portal 2
- Online menus and the co-op lobby now run at full speed (60 FPS instead of 9 FPS, and under 1 FPS in the lobby).

## Other changes
- Network: a socket wait with a time limit no longer blocks the other network calls of the game.
- Silent microphone: when no microphone is available, the emulator now fills its buffers in real time, like a real one.

## Animal Crossing: New Horizons
- Best friends between the emulator and a real Switch: in Animal Crossing, the emulator now uses the same online identity as a Switch linked to the same Nextendo account, so players on Ryujinx and on Switch can become best friends. This turns on together with the matching Nextendo server update; until then, nothing changes.
- Your island in the cloud: this turns on with the Nextendo server update.

## Other changes

- macOS: Artis Impact black screen fixed, kernel range check fixed, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Thai text no longer shows as boxes (gzdemon77).

releases.name: v1.0.0
releases.body:
I am proud to announce the first release of Hades, version 1.0.0!

This first release provides:

  - A complete emulation of the Game Boy Advance (with the exception of most external devices and add-ons)
  - Decent accuracy
  - Game controller support
  - Keys and buttons remapping
  - Quick Saves (also known as Save State)
  - Real Time Clock (RTC) support
  - Color correction & LCD effects
  - Loading games from common archive formats (.zip, .7z, .rar, etc.)

I will now focus my efforts on performances, accuracy and providing support for more video effects and new external devices!

Than you for taking the time to check on Hades~

# PS5PCEM 0.3.4

**This release fixes a launcher regression that prevented games from starting
in packaged installations. Updating both the launcher and runner is recommended.**
It also adds working font rendering, fixes Jurassic Park's font-atlas startup,
implements MemoryPool and AMPR counters, and expands RDNA2 shader support.

These are the changes since **0.3.3**, covering the October 7–9 development
commits. The portable ZIP and per-user installer include the updated launcher,
runner and PKG extractor. All three applications and the installer carry
timestamped SHA-256 Authenticode signatures using the same
**Artur Strazewicz / PS5PCEM** certificate as the previous release.

## Important launcher fix

The launcher could pass its own executable path as the runner's working
directory because a shortened Windows path lacked its terminating zero.
Windows rejected `CreateProcessW` with `ERROR_DIRECTORY` before the game
started. The development `zig-out\bin` layout masked the defect, while ordinary
portable and installed layouts exposed it. The directory is now correctly
terminated.

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 — Release Notes

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.9.8 is a performance release. Nothing in the emulation model changed: every
game still renders the same picture it did in v0.9.9.6, and the same save states still load. What
changed is how much work the CPU and the GPU have to do to get there.

The headline is that the hybrid JIT now translates **more than 80 % of the guest instruction
stream to native x86-64**, the Vulkan renderer stopped paying for a redundant depth write that was
silently disabling hardware Early-Z / Hi-Z culling, and UMA GPUs finally get zero-copy geometry
upload. Together those turn the integrated-GPU experience from "lock it to 496×384" into a picture
that can actually be played at native resolution.

## 📦 Packages

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.8.6a — Windows hotfix

**Windows only.** This release contains a single asset for Windows x64. Everything else is
v0.9.8.6 unchanged.

---

## Why the v0.9.8.6 Windows package refused to start on AMD graphics cards

On Windows, AMD's Vulkan driver reports **128 bytes** of push constants — the amount Vulkan itself
guarantees. Every driver this renderer had been developed against reports 256.

The 3D scene shader packed 208 bytes into that block: the projection matrix, the light parameters
and the fog colour, re-sent on every single draw call. The renderer's device selection therefore
required 256 bytes, found 128, rejected the GPU, and the program exited — the start-up artwork
flashed and disappeared, no settings window, no game, no message. Nothing in the picture was wrong;
the renderer simply refused to open the device.

The report that surfaced this was a Steam Deck running Windows 11, whose AMD APU driver reports 128
as well — but the same limit applies to Radeon cards and Ryzen APUs on Windows generally, not to one
machine.

## What is fixed

**The scene shader now fits in the 128 bytes Vulkan guarantees.** The projection matrix, the light
parameters and t

# Model 3-Vulkan v0.9.8.6x — Linux and macOS

**This release replaces both `v0.9.8.6l` (Linux) and `v0.9.8.6m` (macOS).** It contains three
assets: Linux, macOS for Apple Silicon, and macOS for Intel Macs. There is no Windows package: the
Windows build is unchanged since v0.9.8.6 and does not need this update.

## Fixed in both packages

**The in-game settings panel ignored the mouse and the keyboard on Linux and macOS.**

Press Tab and the panel opened, but nothing in it responded: no hover highlight, no clicks, no arrow
keys, no Enter. The panel's input feed was Windows-only — the whole block that reads the pointer
position, the mouse buttons and the key states sat behind `#ifdef _WIN32`, with no equivalent for the
other platforms, so on Linux and macOS only the mouse wheel was ever delivered. It now reads the

mouse buttons, Ctrl/Shift/Alt and a full key table (arrows, Tab, Enter, Escape, Home/End, Page Up/Down,
Insert/Delete, Backspace, Space, A/C/V/X/Z, digits and the keypad).

releases.body:
## Changes since build 160

Built from nx2 87d84d513c. Build 160 was 2eb5f08. That's 86 merged changes.

> **The yuzu name is gone.** The build system, source folders, Qt frontend, translations, emulator libraries and docs now say Lichii instead of the name inherited from yuzu. Your settings, saves and shader caches are kept: config keys, data folders and cache formats don't change, and the few on-disk names that still carry the old name (the shader cache's file magic, the save-size file inside saves, the import path for yuzu data) stay as they are. The program files are still called `lichii`, `eden-cli` and `eden-room`. On macOS the app's bundle id changed, so macOS asks for camera and input permission again (#1541, #1550, #1551, #1552, #1553, #1544, #1582).

### Big fixes
- **Ocarina of Time: the far forest no longer floats, and Hyrule Field's frame rate is back.** In test builds after build 160, the far pine forest in Hyrule Field and in Kakariko at night was drawn unculled and partly above the ridge, and a spot that ran at 40 fps dropped to 27 fps (RTX 3080). An upstream change that came in with the Eglantine sync (#1462) generated the shader helpers for these foliage programs

releases.name: Lichii nx2 build 160 (2eb5f08)
releases.body:
## Changes since build 150

Built from nx2 2eb5f081c8. Build 150 was 17baed7. That's 30 merged changes.

> **New look.** Lichii now opens in the new **Lichii Dark** theme, and a short **What's new** window explains what moved. You can reopen it from **Help → What's New**, and the old themes are still in the settings.

### Big fixes
- **Yoshi and the Mysterious Book: the 3D world renders.** Three shader forms the game uses were rejected, which left the world black. Built on ggonzalospineli-ops' #1189 and FrsrG's #1284, with ALD/OUT from MythosOfs (#1363).
- **The Duskbloods network test: boots to its menus.** It no longer aborts on memory, and its shader forms are supported. By cerroverb (#552, #851). It still stops at its online checks. It also always uses reactive flushing, gets the DLSS replacement (#828, #637), and has a 3D colour-target clear fix (#638).
- **Ocarina of Time: the guard house freeze is fixed** by a built-in Texture Pool x2 patch (#1313).
- **Mario Kart World: characters and karts are lit correctly.** Read-only compute bindings are sized from their size word (#1333).
- **No more crash when antivirus deletes nxformat.dll.** nxformat 1.0.3 is now built into Lichii.

releases.body:
> **New here or getting bad performance?** Stop the game, then use **Help → Apply Recommended Settings...** to apply the recommended settings in one click. **Help → Restore My Previous Settings** undoes it.

Automatic build of `nx2` at 17baed716da04fd743fbd8f9604bec96eab0a123.

## What changed since build 130

Build 150 was built from nx2 17baed716d. Build 130 was 3dae119. That's 51 merged changes.

## Big fixes
- **Ocarina of Time: white wash / blown-out lighting fixed.** Destroyed GPU memory kept its old backing, so reused memory showed stale pages. Diagnosis and fix by 99ivs, with a safety refresh by PantACRO4life (#1236).
- **Mario Kart World: dark characters and karts fixed.** Compute shaders reading lighting data were cut off at 8 MiB and now see the whole buffer (#1231).
- **Ocarina of Time: out-of-memory crash on Windows.** The texture cache now stays within Windows' memory commit limit (#1210).
- **Ocarina of Time: ocarina crackle fixed** (ADPCM sign) (#1196).
- **Ocarina of Time: dark fairy fountain and Water Temple walls.** These are dumps with damaged texture members. Lichii now serves a stand-in instead of black (#1197).

## New features
- **NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 settings.**

releases.body:
## ⚠️ Delete your old pipeline cache before playing

This build uses a new shader cache (v2). To avoid stutter or problems from leftover caches of older builds, delete each game's old pipeline cache once:

1. In Lichii, right-click the game in your game list.
2. Choose **Remove → Remove All Pipeline Caches** and confirm.
3. Repeat for each game you play.

**Or delete the folder by hand** (close Lichii first):
- **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\eden\cache\shader\`. If you use a portable install, it's `user\cache\shader\` next to `lichii.exe`.
- **Linux:** `~/.cache/eden/shader/`. If you use a portable install, it's `user/cache/shader/` next to the AppImage.

Each game has its own folder, named after its program id (for example `0400486024DEC000` for Ocarina of Time). Delete the folders of the games you play, or the whole `shader` folder.

The first launch after this builds shaders again, so expect some stutter at first. It goes away as the new cache fills, and it stays filled on later launches.

releases.body:
# Hokkaido 0.6.6

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB) and a Galaxy S25 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, 12 GB), both on Android 17. The performance work tested on the S26's Exynos carries over well to Snapdragon.

## New in 0.6.6

- **Pokopia's sky renders.** Under NCE, a game read from memory the GPU had drawn into was treated as a write, which threw the GPU's result away. Such reads now fetch the GPU's data, and reactive flushing is kept on for Pokopia. Both apply to Pokopia only. Thanks to Diriande for the fix (#17), our first outside contribution.

## From 0.6.5

- **Fast Fusion** now gets past its title screen and into races, but at low frame rates (the game runs in slow motion) and with a shimmering image. Before, it crashed right after the splash screen on every phone tested: at 0.5x resolution, render targets were freed while a cached scaling helper still used them.
- **Ocarina of Time on 12 GB phones:** Ocarina of Time will no longer be optimized for 12 GB devices. It needs more memory than a 12 GB phone has free and can be closed for low memory there. 16 GB of RAM is recommended.
- **Speed and memory** (upstream)
  - GPU address space is reuse

# Hokkaido 0.6.4

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB) and a Galaxy S24 (Exynos 2400, Xclipse 940, 8 GB), both on Android 17.

## Highlights

- **Game compatibility** (upstream)
  - A texture slot that is still empty when a shader is built now compiles as a 2D texture. Upstream this fixed Pokémon Legends Z-A's blank screen.
  - Shader translation no longer runs out of stack on Kirby Air Riders' loops.
  - More shaders translate: shifts with a uniform shift amount (SHF), and more texture gather and call forms.
  - Ocarina of Time 1.0 (without the update) works with the "No Sharpening" anti-aliasing setting.
- **Snapdragon:** Adreno's early depth test (LRZ) is turned off where it drew wrong, on Qualcomm's own driver (upstream).
- **Memory** (upstream)
  - ASTC textures with uneven mip levels stay compressed on phones and other GPUs with shared or small memory.
  - A new buffer no longer joins a large buffer it only shares a page with. Upstream this caused slowdowns and a crash on Yoshi's book pages.
  - Memory hints skip placeholder addresses.
- **Stability** (upstream)
  - Closing a game while its shaders load no longer hangs, and the next launch works.

Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S26 (Exynos 2600, Xclipse 960, 12 GB) and a Galaxy S24 (Exynos 2400, Xclipse 940, 8 GB), both on Android 17.

- **Less work per frame for the GPU threads** (upstream):
  - A run of uploads goes to the GPU as one command with one pair of barriers, and later transfers are ordered after earlier copies to the same memory.
  - Each compute dispatch records its barrier in its own command, instead of a separate one.
  - Empty submissions to the GPU are skipped.
- **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time**

  - GPU memory the game destroys is released, and reused memory is refreshed.

  - Threads waiting for the GPU are released when a game stops.

**Prepare on the phone (experimental).** The app can now make a game's pack from your dump on the phone itself. You no longer need a computer.

### How

Copy your dump (or `.nup`) to the phone, open **Anka Native**, tap **Add game**, pick the dump and tap **Prepare**. The app does three things in the background, with a notification:

1. It rewrites the game's code.
2. It scans the game's files for shaders.
3. It translates the shaders.

When it is done, the game's card says Ready.

- **Keep the phone on a charger.** For Ocarina of Time, preparing takes about 3 hours and uses the CPU fully.
- If a step fails, the card says why. Its log is in `<title ID>-work/ondevice/logs` next to the dump. Preparing on a computer still works as before.

- **Code rewrite:** worked, about 3 minutes.

Seven weeks of hardware fidelity work since 0.6.1.

releases.body:
## NeoST 0.6.1 — your settings stay put

A patch release. No new features: **23 defects** found and fixed across five rounds of multi-agent bug hunting, plus a hardware-validation pass on the published packages.

### Settings are saved again

On macOS and on every AppImage, NeoST runs from **read-only media**, so it stores its configuration in your user directory — but it never created that directory, and every setting was silently lost when you closed the emulator. **Five of the eight packages were affected.** Machine profile, video, audio and MIDI setup now survive a restart.

### Also fixed

- **The macOS disk image installs by drag and drop.** It shipped with the app alone, no `Applications` shortcut.
- **The web build ships its licences** (GPL-3.0, GPL-2.0, third-party notices), like every other package.
- **A save-state can no longer be reloaded under a different ROM.** The pairing relied on two bytes of TOS version, which five localisations share, so resuming under the wrong ROM froze the CPU without a word. The state format is now **v19**; v18 and older are refused explicitly, with a message that says why.
- **A malformed `.PRG` can no longer make NeoST read outside its mem

Beta 10 adds **global physical-controller profiles** and improves Mophun sound and game speed.

Open **Settings → Physical controller profiles** to edit the global mapping or create reusable profiles for buttons and both sticks. Assign them to games from the manager or each game's Controls page. Graphics, touch layouts and physical mappings stay independent. ## SkyNetEmu 0.2.4

Source revision: `c57e7f5d7608691bde97bc1c523c22ddf25604c6` (version code 7, version name `0.2.4-stable+c57e7f5`). A small update to 0.2.3.

### Fixes

- **Frame generation is smooth again when the game runs below half the screen's refresh rate.** The FPS counter used to double, but each generated frame and the real one reached the screen on back-to-back refreshes (about 8 ms apart, then a 25 ms gap), so motion looked no smoother than without frame generation. Game profiles and the other registry files are read from the tag `v0.2.4` of the components repository (the same content as `v0.2.3`).

**Counter-Strike 2**
- CS2 starts again on a fresh install. A fix release over [0.2.2](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.2), and the one worth updating for: the lighting is right now.

## Fixed

**Walls lit far too brightly, and the odd shading on the soldiers and on the player's hands.** An instruction of the console's shaders has a vector half and a scalar half, and they run together: both read the registers as they were before the instruction and only then write. The translation wrote the vector's result first, so a scalar that read the very register the vector wrote got the new value instead of the old one.

The game's third light per surface is written exactly that way. Its scalar wants the specular exponent times a logarithm; with the write first it took a dot product instead, and two to the tenth of that became the specular. Every lit stone wall in Mayenne came out white with pink and green speckle, and characters were shaded oddly for the same reason. Eighty of the six hundred shader programs a level draws with have such an instruction, so this shows up all over the game, not only on that wall.

A fix release over [0.2.1](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.1); everything below is on top of what 0.2.1 brought.

## Fixed

**The HUD and the menu still flickered.** 0.2.1 looked at every texture every frame again, but a large one that had been still for a while was only *sampled*: sixty four places out of it. The HUD's fonts, icons and compass are small and change a handful of texels at a time, and the samples missed those changes, so the old picture stayed up for a frame. Everything up to two megabytes is now hashed whole, every frame, and only what is bigger than that falls back to sampling.

**Shadow filtering collapsed.** A texture fetch on the console carries three signed offsets in halves of a texel. The game's shadows are one map fetched four times at the corners of a texel; with the offsets dropped those were four fetches of the same texel, so a surface came out wholly lit or wholly dark instead of softly edged.

# Swap2-Native 0.1.8.5-beta

A new Graphics setting for how the game's memory reaches the GPU, with a new default.

**Install over 0.1.8.4-beta (or any 0.1.5-beta and later).** Games, packs, mods and saves are kept. Nothing is prepared again.

## New

- **GPU memory sharing** (Settings › Graphics, and each game's **Game settings › Graphics**):
  - **Shared buffer**, the new default: the game's memory is shared with the GPU through a buffer the app maps itself.
  - **Direct mapping**, what every version before this one did: the GPU driver maps its memory over the game's.
  - On a GPU driver that has no shared buffer, direct mapping is used whatever the setting says.
- **Why the default changed:** on a Redmagic 11 Air, Zelda was closed by the system every time a scene loaded with direct mapping, on three GPU drivers, and ran on the one driver that uses the shared buffer. On our test phone (POCO F7 Ultra) the shared buffer runs the same scene at 30 to 35 fps, against 27 to 31 with direct mapping.
- **If a game got slower or misbehaves after this update, set it back to Direct mapping** and tell us which phone and GPU driver.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.3
releases.body:
Play your real Sega CD discs. Nothing else in the emulation changed.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.3-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### New

- **Sega CD discs straight from your PC's CD/DVD drive.** Put the disc in,
  choose **File → Open ROM → Sega CD from drive**, and pick the drive. GenX
  reads the game and its CD music from the disc, reading ahead while you play
  so the drive keeps up. A USB drive works too.
- **Changing discs:** use **Sega CD → Swap to disc in drive**, or just put the
  next disc in the drive. GenX swaps it in as a real Sega CD would.
- **Front ends:** `genx.exe E:\` starts the disc in drive E:.

You still need the Sega CD BIOS for the disc's region.

If your drive or a disc doesn't work, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/issues) with the drive's
make and model and the game.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for every change.

Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the exe isn't code-signed.
Choose **More info → Run anyway**.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.2
releases.body:
Sega CD fixes. Nothing else in the emulation changed.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.2-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### Fixed

- **Crash when opening a Sega CD disc.** GenX closed without a message when a
  disc sat near a file or folder whose name has certain characters, such as an
  accent stored as a separate mark (some "Pokémon" names) or Japanese text.
- **Japanese and Southeast Asian Sega CD BIOSes now start.** They used to stop
  on an error such as "This is a PAL-compatible Mega CD for exclusive use in
  Southeast Asia", because GenX always presented itself as a US or European
  console. GenX now becomes the console the BIOS belongs to.
- **Japanese discs get a Japanese BIOS** when your BIOS folder also holds the
  Southeast Asian one. Some BIOS packs name the Southeast Asian BIOS
  `jp_mcd1_9112.bin`, which GenX used to pick first.
- The **BIOS** tab in **Configure** shows the BIOS each region's discs will
  really use.

Thanks to the player who reported the Southeast Asia error.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/blob/main/CHANGEL

Android build of Cemu Plus, a fork of the Cemu Android port with Lossless Scaling frame generation.

### Game updates
- **Use update** in the settings of a game, under Update, turns its installed update off, and the game runs as its base version. It's only shown for games with an update, and applies the next time the game starts. The game card shows the version the game runs as

### Motion sensitivity
- **Motion sensitivity X axis** and **Motion sensitivity Y axis** set how fast turning left and right, and tilting up and down go, from 25% to 500%. releases.name: v2.3 – Faster games, NFL Fever 2004 fix, Linux build, Performance and compatibility release: CPU boost, GPU boost, per-game settings with automatic safe mode, a fix that lets NFL Fever 2004 run, and a first Linux build
releases.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Experimental, unofficial fork of xemu for trying out UI improvements. Not supported by the xemu project: please don't ask about it in xemu's Discord or GitHub.
What's new in v2.3
This release is about speed and game compatibility. The emulation changes are listed here so you know what touches the game itself.
CPU boost and GPU boost (Settings > General > Performance). CPU boost runs the game's SSE math on your PC's processor and trims work in the CPU emulation. GPU boost turns on faster paths in the graphics code, such as skipping textures a shader never reads. Turn either off if a game misbehaves. releases.name: RomSieve 1.1.1
releases.body:
RomSieve 1.1.1 fixes how 1G1R handles games on several floppy disks in the No-Intro DATs, such as those of the Acorn
Archimedes. Your settings, profiles and journals stay as they are, and a sort made with 1.1.0 or 1.0.x can still be
undone.

## Fixes

- **Floppy disk sets kept together.** The No-Intro DATs of floppy disks number the disks `(Disk 1)`, `(Disk 2)`...,
  sometimes with a label: `(Disk 1, Game Disk)`, `(Disk 2 - Courses)`. RomSieve did not read these names as disks of
  one set, so 1G1R could keep some disks of a game and leave out the others. The disks of a set are now kept or left
  out together. Without a total in the name (`(Disk 1 of 3)`), the set counts as many disks as the highest number
  found.

# WinLite v1.4.0

## Overview
A release focused on rendering smoothness, a new X11 server and Steam support.

---

## 🎮 BETA - Steam
- Steam client support added.

---

## 🖥️ X11 server (rewritten in Rust)
The built-in X server has been rewritten from scratch in Rust and now covers much more of the X11 protocol.

**What you get**
- **Stability.** Memory-safe code removes a whole class of crashes and hangs.
- **Better game and launcher compatibility.** Newer screen-configuration (RANDR 1.2) and rendering extensions are supported, so Wine, launchers and games see a more complete environment.
- **Proper mouse cursors.** System cursors are drawn from a built-in cursor set, and colored/semi-transparent and animated cursors are supported.
- **Better frame pacing.** Frame presentation is synchronized with the real display refresh rate and with fences, which gives the renderer and the FPS limiter an accurate clock to work from.
- **Faster window drawing.** The shared frame buffer is locked once per operation instead of repeatedly, and more drawing requests (lines, rectangles, area clears) are handled directly.
- **Input.** Pointer warping now works, which matters for games that recenter th

releases.name: v1.0.8
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.8: big games run much faster

### What's new
- **Games with very large buffers run much faster.** 1.0.7 uploaded every recently used buffer whole each frame, which for a game like Teardown meant over 3 GB per frame. Now only small buffers (up to 4 MB) are uploaded that way; large ones are tracked by page again. Teardown on a PS4 Pro went from under 1 FPS to about 2.4 FPS. DREDGE keeps its 1.0.7 speed and clean sound.
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0032).

### Teardown and other big games: more GPU memory
Teardown also needs the GPU to be allowed up to 5 GB of system RAM, or it stops with GPU out of memory. Use the `bootargs.txt` of [PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-5](https://github.com/blue0x1/ps4-multiboot/releases/tag/v1.5.0-beta.5) (copy it to `/data/linux/boot/` over FTP), or add `amdgpu.gttsize=5120 ttm.pages_limit=1310720` to the end of the line in your own.

### Update
Settings, System, Software update. No restart is needed. Coming from 1.0.6 or earlier, it installs 1.0.7 first, which also updates the PS4 Mesa (see the 1.0.7 notes).

From 1.0.3 or earlier, start the update once by hand (see the README's Changelog).

### New ins

releases.name: v1.0.7
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.7: faster games, smooth cover changes

### What's new
- **Faster games.** The emulator uploads buffers to the GPU in batches and waits on it less often. DREDGE on a PS4 Pro went from about 12 to 13–28 FPS, and 44–50 FPS in lighter views, and its sound no longer crackles.
- **A new emulator build** (KytyPS5 589bd14 with EmuFive patches 0001–0031): better memory use, GPU caches and shader translation, on top of the speed-ups above.
- **Smooth cover changes on the home screen.** Moving between games now changes the cover smoothly. Pick the effect in Settings, Appearance, Motion, Cover change. There are 11: fade, slide, zoom, wipe, dark, parallax, blinds, doors, push, iris and pixelate.
- **New PS4 Mesa.** The update installs the PS4 Mesa of PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-4, which is needed for all 4 GPU engines on the PS4 Pro (below).

### Update
1. Optional: copy `ps4-mesa.tar.xz` from [PS4 Multiboot v1.5.0-beta-4](https://github.com/blue0x1/ps4-multiboot/releases/tag/v1.5.0-beta.4) to `/user/home/` over FTP. The update takes it from there; without it, the PS4 needs to be online and downloads it (about 45 MB).
2. Settings, System, Software update. No restart is needed.

releases.name: v1.0.4
releases.body:
## EmuFive 1.0.4

- Fixed: Software update in Settings did not start ("The update did not start.") (#16).
- Fixed: with EmuFive installed on a USB drive, games on a second USB drive were not found (#15).

### Updating from 1.0.3 or earlier

The old Software update cannot start, so start this update once by hand:

1. In EmuFive, turn on **SSH login** in Settings and connect the PS4 to the internet.
2. From a PC on the same network: `ssh ps5@<PS4 address>` (password `ps5` unless you changed it).
3. Run:
   ```bash
   sudo systemd-run --unit=emufive-update --collect /opt/ps5-on-ps4/bin/ps5-update install
   ```
4. Wait a few minutes, then restart from the home screen.

It installs every update you are missing (from 1.0.0 or 1.0.1 that includes 1.0.2's browser packages, about 110 MB). From 1.0.4 on, Software update in Settings works.

### New installs

`ps5-ps4-rootfs.tar.xz` below has 1.0.4 built in (install steps in the README).

releases.body:
# Lichii-Enhanced v1.0.0: first public release

Lichii-Enhanced is a fork of [Lichii](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii) focused on usability: easier setup, built-in upscaling, non-destructive modding and more reliable online play. This is the first public release.

> **Platform:** Windows 10/11 x64 only. Distributed as a `.zip` archive. Other platforms are not available yet.

## Highlights

### 🖼️ Built-in upscalers
Upscaling is now part of the renderer; no external injectors or wrappers are needed.

- New post-process stage at the end of the Vulkan frame (compute shaders), running after game rendering and before swapchain presentation
- Filters: Nearest, Bilinear, Bicubic, FSR 1.0 (EASU + RCAS), SGSR
- Configurable render scale and sharpness (RCAS strength)
- Per-game profiles stored in `config/custom/<title-id>.ini`
- Optional anti-aliasing pass before upscaling

releases.name: recomp-launcher 0.3.0
releases.body:
### Added
- The installer shows its version (the game's tag, or the short commit for a
  build off a branch) in the window's corner and title, and on start asks
  GitHub for the game's newest release: a newer one gets a download button.
  Offline it says nothing.
- `game.files` takes globs: `*.iso` makes a folder holding a disc image the
  game, for a title whose setup takes an image rather than an install.
- `installer.yml` takes `platforms` (default `windows linux macos`), so a
  Windows-only game doesn't publish installers that can't build it.
- A `game.files` entry may be alternatives, `a|b`: `HOVER.EXE|hover*.zip` is
  the game's folder or a folder holding a zip of it.

- The Windows installer carries version info and a manifest, and a release
  has `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so antivirus heuristics and players can check it.
- A log of why the installer stopped (`%APPDATA%\recomp-launcher\launcher.log`
  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

### Fixed
- On Windows a step line after a blank line was glued to the line before it
  (ConPTY skips the blank line with a cursor move), so the bar missed that step.

releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.1
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.1 updates the bundled AnyPS5 core from v0.1.2 to **[v0.1.4](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/releases/tag/v0.1.4)**.

## Changes
- **AnyPS5 core v0.1.4**: the bundled relinker and system libraries now come from the latest upstream release. Existing installs switch to it automatically the next time Studio starts, and each game receives the new libraries on its next launch.
- **Relink hint**: Studio now remembers which core relinked each game. If a game was relinked with an earlier core, the launch log says so and suggests relinking it in Relinker Studio if it fails to start.
- **Verified core downloads**: the bundled core is checked against the SHA-256 checksums AnyPS5 publishes for the release; a mismatch stops the build.
- The NID inspector's "Python 3 not found" message now points to the correct re-audit button.

## After updating
If a game that worked before no longer starts, open **Relinker Studio** and relink it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ramsforge/AnyPS5-Studio/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1

releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.0
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.0 is the biggest update so far: full controller support, playtime tracking, safer handling of your game folders, a faster app that works offline, and a round of security hardening.

## Highlights

### Full controller navigation
- Use the D-pad / left stick to move around every screen (menus, Settings, dialogs, setup and the launcher). Cross selects, Circle goes back, L1 / R1 switch tabs.
- On the game row, Left / Right still pick a game and Cross plays it; press Down to reach the game's buttons.
- Studio ignores the controller while you are playing a game, so button presses never reach Studio behind it.
- Controller rumble now follows the Haptic Feedback setting.
- Arrow keys and Escape work the same way on the keyboard.

### Playtime tracking
- Total playtime and your last session are recorded for every game and shown on the home screen.

### Safer game folders
- Studio only reorganizes folders that actually contain a PS5 title, and no longer moves game assets just because their name looks like a backup (for example `*.baked`).
- Backups are never overwritten, and every change is recorded. **Restore Original Folder Layout** (game details panel) moves everything b

releases.name: Winlator 中文版 (Wine 11) v1.0.0
releases.body:
# Winlator 中文版 (Wine 11) v1.0.0

基于 [Winlator 11.1](https://github.com/brunodev85/winlator) 深度定制:

## 主要变化
- **Wine 10.10 -> Wine 11.15**: 移植 brunodev85 全部定制补丁 (Android 存储符号链接、GPU 信息上报、X11 窗口属性等) 至 Wine 11.15 新 WoW64 模式 (x86_64-unix + i386/x86_64 双架构 PE)
- **esync -> fastsync**: 移除旧 esync 机制, 使用 Wine 11 原生 fastsync, 同步性能更好
- **完整中文支持**:
  - Android 界面全面中文翻译 (values-zh-rCN)
  - 内置 Noto Sans CJK SC 中文字体 + fontconfig 中文别名
  - rootfs 注入 zh_CN.UTF-8 locale (glibc + X11)
  - Wine 前缀注册表中文字体替换 (宋体/SimSun -> Noto Sans CJK SC)
  - 新建容器默认中文环境

## 下载安装
直接下载下方 APK (约 325 MB) 安装即可, 无需额外组件。首次启动会自动解包 rootfs。

## 技术说明

# Winlator 中文版 (Wine 11) v1.0.0

基于 [Winlator 11.1](https://github.com/brunodev85/winlator) 深度定制:

## 主要变化
- **Wine 10.10 -> Wine 11.15**: 移植 brunodev85 全部定制补丁 (Android 存储符号链接、GPU 信息上报、X11 窗口属性等) 至 Wine 11.15 新 WoW64 模式 (x86_64-unix + i386/x86_64 双架构 PE)
- **esync -> fastsync**: 移除旧 esync 机制, 使用 Wine 11 原生 fastsync, 同步性能更好
- **完整中文支持**:
  - Android 界面全面中文翻译 (values-zh-rCN)
  - 内置 Noto Sans CJK SC 中文字体 + fontconfig 中文别名
  - rootfs 注入 zh_CN.UTF-8 locale (glibc + X11)
  - Wine 前缀注册表中文字体替换 (宋体/SimSun -> Noto Sans CJK SC)
  - 新建容器默认中文环境

## 下载安装
直接下载下方 APK (约 325 MB) 安装即可, 无需额外组件。首次启动会自动解包 rootfs。

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.2 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Restores compatibility with third-party native mods. If mods failed to load, or loaded and then force-closed the game, this is the fix.

### Fixed

* **Mods failed to load with "Unknown mod load failure".** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  Adding the companion's slot I/II buttons pushed `BTN_R` to `1 << 8` and widened `daAlink_c::itemTriggerCheck` / `itemButtonCheck` from `u8` to `u16`. That changes the mangled names, so mods built against upstream Dusklight could not resolve them and failed at `dlopen`. The upstream symbols are re-exported as forwarders that translate the button numbering as well as the width — upstream's `BTN_B` is `BTN_S2` here, so widening alone would have routed a sword check to a slot button.

  Measured against three mods: only 2 of 842, 762 and 55 game-symbol imports were unresolved.

* **The game force-closed when a loaded mod ran.**

  Ten `ConfigVar`s had been inserted into the middle of `UserSettings` (`showPipelineProgress`, the seven `dualScreen*`, `configMigration`, `guideEnabled`), shifting every later setting by ~450 bytes. Mods compile `settings.<group>.<var>` to a byte offset, so every settings read in every mod silently po

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.1 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Patch release for **Dual-Screen 3.0**. No gameplay or dual-screen changes — the native code is identical to 3.0.

### Fixed

* **Cosmetics, Luau Support and Randomizer were missing from the Android build.** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  The Android CMake presets listed only the `dusklight` target, so the `dusklight_mods` aggregate target never ran and `bundled_mods/` was never produced. Gradle packs that directory into `assets/mods`, so the APK shipped with no bundled mod packages at all. Mods that depend on the Luau runtime could not load either.

  All three packages are now present: `cosmetics`, `luau_runtime` and `randomizer`.

  CI was never affected — `build.yml` builds `dusklight_mods` as its own explicit `--target` step. This only broke preset-driven local builds.

releases.name: Dual-Screen 2.7 (based on Dusklight v1.4.1)
releases.body:
Properly fixes the texture pack stutter this time, the renderer now streams replacements in the background instead of loading them mid-frame. Also adds an Ooccoo button to the map so she does not need an item slot, and cleans up saved guides.

## Using the Ooccoo button
Appears in the bottom-left of the map window whenever you are carrying her, no equipping needed.
1. Open the companion's **Map** page.
2. Tap **Ooccoo** (Sr. in a dungeon) or **Ooccoo Jr.** (out in the field).

Your I / II slots are not disturbed, the button borrows one for half a second and puts it straight back.

## New
* **Ooccoo on the map**, one tap to leave a dungeon or return, without giving up an item slot.

## Fixes
* **Fixed: stutter with texture packs on the intro, cutscenes and area changes**, replacements were still being read and uploaded during the frame. The renderer is now up to date with upstream, which loads them on background threads, shows a low-resolution version first and limits how much reaches the GPU per frame. On an 8 GB pack the memory spike that caused it dropped from 1100 MB to 300 MB, and Android no longer starts reclaiming memory mid-intro.
* **Fixed: guide reader stalling on images**
